artifacts.summary: 6-phase closure of the deploy-pending completion loop: honest exit-6 bookkeeping in the batch postflight, guaranteed cycle_modified_files accumulation (already-satisfied, characterized live), a widened Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint predicate, an end-to-end demonstration transcript, D6 residual retirement, and the post-unwind replay-path documentation -- with no third automated deploy-trigger site added.

completion_data.completion_summary: Closed the deploy-pending (exit 6) completion loop for the batch /orchestrate engine: the postflight now honestly reports a deploy-pending refusal (verdict=defer, paused commit) instead of falsely claiming completion, cycle_modified_files accumulation across a refusal was characterized and confirmed already-sound, and the Inter-Cycle Redeploy Checkpoint's trigger predicate was widened so any agent-system/extensions/** touch converges automatically on the following cycle -- demonstrated end to end with no manual deploy or reconcile step, and with no new automated deploy-trigger site added.

memory_candidates.content: When a gated automation site already has the override signal it needs but the signal is scoped too narrowly (e.g. computed only inside a narrower conditional branch), the fix is often to HOIST the existing computation out of that branch and WIDEN the branch condition with an OR -- not to add a new trigger site. This closes the gap while reusing all existing downstream machinery (ledger consults, idempotence guards) unchanged. Concretely: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's deploy_pending_any override already existed and already forced the ledger decision to run, but was computed only inside `matched_count -gt 0`; hoisting it out and widening to `matched_count -gt 0 OR deploy_pending_any` closed the D6 residual with zero new deploy-trigger sites.

Before implementing a fix for a suspected accumulation/gating bug, write a characterization test against UNMODIFIED code first and record the result. In this task, the dispatch assumed cycle_modified_files accumulation was gated on a refused postflight write, but a real exit-6-refusal fixture test proved the block was already ungated (no `set -e`, no dispatch_status/verdict guard) -- the bug hypothesis was wrong, and a redundant fix was avoided. The characterization test itself became permanent regression-anchor coverage rather than throwaway diagnostic work.

For an 'end-to-end, not asserted' acceptance criterion on a bash-orchestrated batch engine, build a scripted demonstration harness that copies the REAL production scripts (not stubs of the logic under test) into an isolated mktemp -d fixture repo, stubs only the genuinely external boundary (deploy-headless.sh/verify-deploy.sh), and chains multiple real script invocations to reproduce the multi-cycle sequence. A deploy-headless.sh stub that performs a behaviorally realistic action (e.g. syncing .claude-extensions.json's recorded source_git_head to match the fixture source repo's actual HEAD) makes the demonstration prove the SAME re-evaluation logic a real redeploy would trigger, not just that a stub was called.
